Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

please also inspect the ignored files list because last month it included temporary preview images from the map application there are about eighty preview images in the archive folder and only the application cache should be ignored the folder named exports contains the approved map pdfs and it must remain included in sync the assistant said quote i thought the exports folder was just a local copy end quote but it is the copy the print shop uses so check its status on at least one mac and one windows machine without opening or changing any pdf files if a machine says the folder is online only record that wording and ask me whether to download it do not assume online only means missing

one last detail i almost said to clear the client history but no leave the history alone we may need it to trace the duplicate folders later and the office manager wants the original screenshots attached to the log rather than pasted into the project folder please keep the log in the existing operations folder which is already shared with the office manager and me do not create another shared folder for the maintenance notes if the client asks for a restart after the profile change record the prompt and ask me before restarting any machine at the end of the window let me know which checks are complete and which are waiting on my decision but do not present a planned action as a completed one", "output": "We have been using the shared folder sync client at the North Quay Design Studio since the new laptops arrived in April, and I am dictating a request for the next maintenance window, not a report on something already done. The folder is called Field Survey, and it holds the current maps, interview notes, and scanned permits for the Harbor Path project. Nine people have access, including me and two contractors who work from home. The client runs on macOS on six machines and Windows on three. The folder is about eighteen gigabytes, and the client shows roughly twelve thousand files. The old laptops are still listed in the device panel, but they are not supposed to sync anymore.

On Monday morning, the status page showed that the desktop had uploaded a large batch while the other machines were trying to download the same batch, and that made the shared connection slow for everyone. The connection is normally about forty megabits per second down and ten megabits per second up, but the studio uses the upload side for video calls and sending print proofs, so a long upload can be more disruptive than a slow download. I checked the activity list and saw three duplicate folders called Field Survey Copy. The newest one was created by the client after the laptop named Edit Room 2 woke from sleep. I do not know whether the other two were made by a person or by an earlier sync conflict, so please leave their contents alone until we compare them.

For the next window, please change the upload limit setting to six megabits per second during working hours and keep the existing unlimited setting outside those hours. The setting key is on its own line here:
sync.limit_uploads
Please apply that setting to the shared folder profile, not to every folder in the client. The working hours are nine in the morning to five thirty in the afternoon, local time, Monday through Friday, and the studio is in the Pacific time zone. I want the upload limit to affect new transfers and retries alike, but it should not cancel a transfer that is already in progress. If the client can only apply the limit after the current transfer finishes, then wait for it rather than restarting it. I am asking for the limit to be set, not saying that it has been set.

1. Check that the nine active accounts still have access and that the two contractors are not members of the billing group, because they only need the project folder.
2. Confirm that the old devices named Studio iMac 2018 and Travel Book 2019 are paused before removing either device record.
3. Review the three duplicate folders against the team drive copy from last Friday and write down which files differ.
4. Check the sync client version on the six Macs and three Windows machines, and note any machine that is more than one minor release behind. Do not update the old device records just because they are visible in the list. The office manager said, “Please tell me before anyone removes a folder that might contain the signed permit scans.” That matters because the signed permits are not easy to replace.

We had one earlier conflict where a drawing called Pier Entrance Final was replaced by a copy with the same name but an older revision date. The designer restored it from the project archive, and the current version is dated May 4. This time, do not choose a winner based only on the filename or the date; compare the file size and the revision field in the drawing application too. If those disagree, flag the file for me and leave both copies in place. The architect is reviewing the entrance layout on Friday afternoon, not Thursday, so the comparison needs to be ready before Friday at noon. I corrected the day because the first date I said was wrong.

The sync client has a bandwidth panel that reports recent use in five-minute intervals and a separate history panel that keeps fourteen days of activity. Please save a screenshot of the bandwidth panel before the setting changes and another one after the new limit has been active for at least thirty minutes. The screenshots should show the machine name and local time, but not any personal email addresses. The admin console also records the time of each setting change, so note that time in the maintenance log. If the console uses UTC, write UTC beside the time rather than converting it by guesswork. Do not treat a quiet five-minute interval as proof that the limit is working.

If one of the contractors is still uploading a folder at the start of the window, leave that session running and message me the folder name and approximate remaining size before changing the profile. If both contractors have finished, continue with the profile change once the duplicate folders have been checked. If either one is still active, wait until the upload completes unless the client reports a stalled transfer for more than twenty minutes; then pause and ask me before resuming. I am not asking anyone to delete a stalled file or to change the project folder permissions while investigating this. The condition about an active contractor upload matters because the current print proofs are due to the client the next morning.

Please also inspect the ignored files list, because last month it included temporary preview images from the map application. There are about eighty preview images in the archive folder, and only the application cache should be ignored. The folder named Exports contains the approved map PDFs, and it must remain included in sync. The assistant said, “I thought the Exports folder was just a local copy,” but it is the copy the print shop uses, so check its status on at least one Mac and one Windows machine without opening or changing any PDF files. If a machine says the folder is online only, record that wording and ask me whether to download it. Do not assume online only means missing.

After the checks are finished, leave the activity history intact and add a short entry to the maintenance log with the setting key, the selected profile, the date, and the names of the machines that were checked. Include any unresolved duplicate or version issue, and say whether the contractor upload condition delayed the change. If no issue is found, write that no issue was found in the log only after the checks are complete. Do not send a message to the whole studio group, because the team is already using that channel for the permit review. Send the log entry to me and the office manager instead. The maintenance window is planned for Wednesday at seven in the evening and should take about forty minutes, but if the file comparison is unfinished at the end of that time, stop before removing devices or duplicate folders and tell me what remains.

One last detail: I almost said to clear the client history, but no, leave the history alone; we may need it to trace the duplicate folders later. The office manager wants the original screenshots attached to the log rather than pasted into the project folder. Please keep the log in the existing operations folder, which is already shared with the office manager and me. Do not create another shared folder for the maintenance notes. If the client asks for a restart after the profile change, record the prompt and ask me before restarting any machine. At the end of the window, let me know which checks are complete and which are waiting on my decision, but do not present a planned action as a completed one."}]
